extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for adopting, publishing, and implementing grievance procedures to investigate and resolve complaints of sex discrimination and sex-based harassment under Title IX, including who may file complaints, required procedural elements, and limits on Title IX Coordinator authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and equitable resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of sex discrimination complaints (reiterating the longstanding requirement since 1975).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary delay in the resolution of sex discrimination complaints; promptness is critical (especially for elementary and secondary recipients) and serves Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate. The final regulations preserve this requirement and make minor clarifying edits to the phrasing (e.g., order of 'prompt and equitable' and adding 'resolution of').

rubrics_metrics.name: Written grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures must be in writing (§§106.45(a)(1) and 106.46(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written procedures are important to inform a recipient of its obligations under Title IX and to clearly explain required grievance procedures so all parties and the institution have clear guidance for processes that lead to fair and reliable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural protections tailored to context
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must provide appropriate procedural protections that account for the age, maturity, and level of independence of students in various educational settings, and the particular contexts of employees and third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt procedures that are sensitive to the differing needs of elementary, secondary, and postsecondary settings and to employees and third parties; ensure protections are calibrated to the setting so processes are fair and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reliability of outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include basic requirements to ensure transparency and reliability in outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations enumerate provisions designed to ensure a fair process (discussed elsewhere in the preamble), and recipients should implement them to increase transparency and produce reliable determinations of whether sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with statutory authority and case law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's grievance-procedure provisions are adopted within its authority under 20 U.S.C. 1682 and are intended to be consistent with Title IX, the U.S. Constitution, contract law, State law (to the extent not preempted), and relevant case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department has reviewed relevant case law and determined that the procedures in §§106.45 and 106.46 are consistent with applicable authorities; recipients should interpret and apply the regulations in a manner consistent with governing court decisions and the Department's delegated authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: recipient is not a respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complaint challenges a recipient's policy or practice, the recipient is not considered a 'respondent' for purposes of the individual-respondent procedural rights in §106.45(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that provisions in §106.45 related to a respondent apply only to complaints alleging an individual violated a recipient's prohibition on sex discrimination. The language does not suggest respondents lack protection from sex discrimination generally; recipients must still implement applicable parts of §106.45 for complaints against the recipient itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make a sex-based harassment complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A sex-based harassment complaint may only be made by a 'complainant' (an individual alleged to have been subjected to sex discrimination), a parent/guardian/other authorized legal representative with the legal right to act on behalf of a complainant, or, in limited circumstances, the Title IX Coordinator (§§106.45(a)(2)(i)-(iii), 106.44(f)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation is designed to protect complainant autonomy in deeply personal harassment matters. The Title IX Coordinator may initiate only in narrow, specified circumstances; otherwise only the aggrieved person (or their authorized representative) should trigger sex-based harassment grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make complaints of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints of sex discrimination that are not sex-based harassment may be filed by: any student or employee; any person other than a student or employee who was participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged discrimination; and the persons listed in (i)-(iii) above (§106.45(a)(2)(iv)(A)-(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broader class is intended to allow reporting about policies, practices, or community-wide harms (e.g., retaliation, failures to make reasonable modifications, discriminatory policies). The final regulations clarify that the participation/attempting-to-participate qualifier applies only to non-students/non-employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on bystander complaints for sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who merely observes or becomes aware of potential discrimination cannot make a complaint of sex-based harassment unless they personally experienced a hostile environment or otherwise qualify as a complainant or authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals who witness conduct that creates a hostile environment for them may make a complaint on their own behalf; uninvolved observers with no connection to the institution who did not experience a hostile environment cannot initiate sex-based harassment complaints. The preamble cites case law recognizing that bystanders can be subject to a hostile environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator authority to initiate proceedings (limited and conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator may initiate a complaint in the absence of a complainant only after determining the alleged conduct 'presents an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant or other person, or that conduct as alleged prevents the recipient from ensuring equal access based on sex to its education program or activity' (§106.44(f)(1)(v)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In making this fact-specific determination the Title IX Coordinator must consider, at a minimum, factors listed in §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(1)-(8): (1) the complainant's request not to proceed; (2) the complainant's reasonable safety concerns about proceeding; (3) risk of additional acts of sex discrimination if not initiated; (4) severity of the alleged discrimination (including whether removal or other discipline might be required); (5) age and relationship of the parties, including whether respondent is an employee; (6) scope of alleged discrimination (pattern, ongoing, or multiple individuals); (7) availability of evidence to assist a decisionmaker; and (8) whether the recipient could end the alleged discrimination and prevent recurrence without initiating grievance procedures. These factors help balance complainant autonomy with safety and access concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of individual respondents when allegations relate to recipient policy or practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complaint alleges an individual engaged in sex discrimination based on actions taken in accordance with a recipient's policy or practice, the recipient must treat the individual as a respondent and comply with the parts of §106.45 that apply to respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such complaints may involve factual questions about whether the individual was following policy, what actions were taken, and potential disciplinary sanctions. The recipient may decide whether to amend the complaint to be against the recipient or proceed against the individual based on the original complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of grievance procedures (enumerated components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include specific procedural elements referenced across §§106.45 and 106.46, including conflicts of interest and bias safeguards (§106.45(b)(2)), notice of allegations and written notice (§106.45(c), §106.46(c)), complaint investigation (§§106.45(f), 106.46(e)), evaluating allegations and assessing credibility (§§106.45(g), 106.46(f)), live hearings (§106.46(g)), and standard of proof (§106.45(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure grievance procedures incorporate these elements to promote fairness, allow meaningful participation by parties, permit credibility determinations where necessary, and produce reliable outcomes. The preamble cites these provisions as central to consistent, lawful grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State law compliance and federal preemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may comply with State law requirements to the extent they do not conflict with the final Title IX regulations; in the event of an actual conflict, the federal regulations have preemptive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in §§106.45 or 106.46 prevents a recipient from honoring contractual obligations or state-mandated grievance procedures that align with the federal requirements; when conflicts arise, federal law/regulation governs. Recipients should aim to comply with both where feasible.
